text: RESULT v1 | k1485e6e779 | Disaster Recovery Strategy for Multi-Region Enterprise Data Centers ⏎ Replication: Primary data center replicates synchronously every 15 minutes to two geographically separated failover regions (Region B and Region C), each in a distinct seismic/grid zone. Replication uses encrypted snapshots with checksum validation on arrival. Retention: 24 hourly, 7 daily, 4 weekly snapshots per region, stored in region-local object storage plus one write-once archive tier for compliance. ⏎ Failover targets: Region B (adjacent continent, low latency) and Region C (distant continent, full isolation). Either can assume full production load. ⏎ Restoration sequence (automated, no manual intervention): ⏎ 1. Detect primary failure via heartbeat loss across three independent probes (90-second threshold). ⏎ 2. Quorum vote by Region B and C controllers declares disaster. ⏎ 3. Halt replication jobs; freeze last validated snapshot. ⏎ 4. Data validation: run checksum and schema-integrity verification on the latest snapshot; if corrupt, roll back to previous validated snapshot. ⏎ 5. Provision compute and network in the elected failover region from infrastructure-as-code templates. ⏎ 6. Restore databases and services from validated snapshot; replay transaction logs to the last consistent state. ⏎ 7. Re-run end-to-end service health checks (API, auth, database read/write). ⏎ 8. Redirect DNS/global load balancer to the failover region. ⏎ 9. Emit compliance audit log recording timestamps for every step. ⏎ 10. On primary recovery, reverse-replicate back and fail back during a scheduled window. ⏎ RTO: under one hour. Budget: detection 2 min, validation 10 min, provisioning 15 min, restore 20 min, health checks 8 min, DNS cutover 5 min = 60 min worst case; typical RTO ~45 minutes. RPO: 15 minutes maximum data loss, per the synchronous replication schedule. ⏎ Compliance: all steps automated and logged; no manual approval gates; encryption in transit and at rest; archive tier immutable for mandated retention period.
